reasons: F01, F02, F03: no material weakness and an unqualified auditor ICFR opinion indicate controls the auditor judged effective.
F05, F06, F07, F14, F15: no auditor change, no disagreements, no prior-period correction and stable CEO/CFO leadership, so none of the usual governance red flags are present.
F16, F17, F18, F19: no SEC inquiry, class action, other government investigation or covenant breach/waiver.
R08, R19: negative total accruals and operating cash flow at or above net income suggest earnings are backed by cash, which argues against aggressive income-boosting accruals.
R09, R17: Beneish M-score and Dechow F-score are both below their manipulation thresholds.

R01, R18: receivables days are normal and receivables are growing slower than sales, with no sign of channel stuffing or premature revenue (F10 no return rights or bill-and-hold; F09 no significant unbilled/contract assets).

R02, R04, R06, R07: declining sales and gross margin, SG&A rising faster than sales and rising leverage show operating deterioration. Combined with F20 (incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS) and F21 (capital raise in year or planned), this creates some pressure or motive to manage earnings.

R03, R13: an elevated asset quality index and a high soft-asset share (>75%) mean more of the balance sheet depends on judgment (e.g. goodwill and intangibles, capitalized costs). This adds impairment and capitalization risk, though F24 shows CAM topics only as 'other'.
F08, F26: revenue recognized mainly over time involves estimates, and non-GAAP emphasis adds some presentation risk. Both are modest concerns without other corroborating signals.
